title: Oat and Honey Flapjacks
subtitle: Chewy, golden flapjacks with just three ingredients
excerpt: These flapjacks come together quickly and need almost no equipment. The honey gives a deep caramel flavour and the oats bake into a satisfying chew. Cut them while still warm for clean squares.
sourceNotes: Flapjacks are a British traybake with roots in wartime economy baking. The base of oats, fat, and sweetener has been a storecupboard staple since the mid-twentieth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap individual squares in cling film and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature for 1 hour.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and use a larger tin. Bake time stays the same.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Flapjacks keep in an airtight tin for up to 5 days.

content.text: Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the tin before baking. Loose, fluffy oats will crumble once cool.
Heat the oven to 180C. Grease a 20cm square baking tin and line with baking paper.
Put the butter and honey in a large saucepan. Melt over a low heat, stirring until smooth.
Remove from the heat. Tip in the oats and stir well until every oat is coated.
Tip the mixture into the prepared tin. Press it down firmly with the back of a spoon.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden at the edges.
Leave in the tin for 5 minutes. Cut into 16 squares while still warm.
Leave to cool completely in the tin before lifting out.

items.cause: The mixture was not pressed down firmly enough before baking.
items.fix: Press harder next time. Cut while still warm.

items.cause: Overbaked or too much honey relative to butter.
items.fix: Reduce bake time by 3 minutes and check early.

items.symptom: Flapjacks are soggy in the middle.
items.fix: Return to oven for 5 minutes and test edges for firmness.
